summary: South Africa's public procurement programme continues, but corporate PPAs are now driving most new utility-scale solar and wind, and behind-the-meter solar exceeds 7 GW. Transmission constraints are the main barrier, and wind bids have been rejected for lack of grid capacity.

access.reason: The renewable IPP procurement programme runs bid windows, and since 2023 private generators of any size are exempt from licensing, though they must register.

build.reason: About 23 wind projects in bid window 6 were not selected because of grid capacity constraints, and the grid remains fragile.

stability.reason: The 2024 coalition government continues the programme, but transmission and affordability problems threaten long-term stability.

direction.reason: Projects are moving from public procurement to corporate PPAs, which were expected to support most 2026 additions.

access.reason: Corporate buyers were expected to support 73% of utility-scale solar and wind added in 2026, more than public procurement.

build.reason: Behind-the-meter solar has grown past 7 GW, but grid-connected projects face transmission limits.

stability.reason: The 2023 licensing changes opened private generation to businesses.

direction.reason: Corporate PPAs are outpacing public procurement for the first time in 2026.
